fullDescription:
An evening that splits neatly in two: sunset over Railay's limestone headlands, then a swim in water that lights up around you.

The boat leaves Ao Nang in the late afternoon and crosses to the Railay peninsula, which has no road access at all. The karsts that make Railay one of the world's great climbing walls turn orange and then deep red as the sun drops behind Phra Nang, and the beach empties as the day-trippers head back. You get the stretch of sand at close to its quietest.

After dark the boat moves to calm water and the guide gets everyone in. The glow comes from dinoflagellates, single-celled plankton that emit light when the water around them is disturbed, so every kick and hand-sweep leaves a trail of blue-green sparks. It is a real phenomenon and not a nightly guarantee: the display is strongest on dark nights around the new moon, and weakest when the moon is full or the sea is churned up. Ask about the moon phase when you pick a date.

Barracudas Tour runs this trip and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is treated as final. The price covers your guide, a snack box, beach mat, drinking water, a fruit platter, life jacket, accident insurance and transfers in the Ao Nang area.

Bring a towel and something dry to change into. Four hours, departing from Ao Nang, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Sunset from Railay, reachable only by boat
Swim in bioluminescent plankton after dark
Brightest on dark nights near the new moon
Guide, snack box, fruit and drinking water included
Ao Nang transfers and life jackets provided

fullDescription:
Two hours on the red-dirt tracks behind Ao Nang, finishing in a freshwater pool.

Krabi's coastline gets all the attention, but a few kilometres inland the landscape turns into rubber and oil-palm plantation cut through with clay trails. That is where this ride goes. After a briefing and a short practice loop you follow the guide through plantation tracks, across shallow water crossings and past limestone outcrops that rise straight out of the fields. The trails hold their shape in dry season and get genuinely muddy from May onwards, which most riders find is the better half of the fun.

The ride breaks at a natural swimming spot to rinse off the dust. Krabi's inland water is spring-fed and stays cool even in April, which is the point of scheduling the swim at the end rather than the start.

No licence is needed and no experience is assumed; the guide sets the pace to the slowest rider in the group. Wear clothes and shoes you do not mind ruining, because you will not stay clean.

Krabi tour runs this and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers hotel pick-up and drop-off, the ATV itself, a guide, fresh fruit, drinking water and accident insurance.

Two hours including transfers, picking up in the Ao Nang area, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Plantation and clay trails behind Ao Nang
Freshwater swim stop at the end of the ride
No licence or experience needed
Hotel pick-up and drop-off included
Fruit, water, guide and accident insurance

fullDescription:
A full day across Phang Nga Bay covering three very different islands, with the Hong Island viewpoint as the centrepiece.

Koh Hong's draw is its lagoon: a near-enclosed pool of shallow green water ringed by limestone walls, reached through a narrow gap that boats can only enter at certain tides. The viewpoint above it is a steep staircase climb, and the reward is the shape of the whole bay laid out below. Laem Had Beach, on the island's northern tip, is a sand spit that runs out into the water and shifts with the tide, which is why photographs of it never quite match.

Naka Yai sits closer to Phuket and is greener and much less visited, with a long shallow beach good for an unhurried swim. Pakbia is tiny, essentially a sandbar with a fringe of trees, and is the stop most people remember for the colour of the water rather than anything on land.

Snorkelling happens where conditions allow, and lunch is served on the island. Nine hours covers a lot of water, so expect a full day rather than a gentle one.

Best Exotic runs this trip and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers all three island visits, the viewpoint, snorkelling, lunch on the island and the Laem Had sandbank.

National park entry is collected separately at the pier unless the operator confirms otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Hong Island lagoon and the viewpoint climb
Laem Had sandbank, which moves with the tide
Naka Yai and Pakbia, both far quieter
Snorkelling and lunch served on the island
Nine-hour day across Phang Nga Bay

fullDescription:
A five-hour evening trip built around two things you cannot see in daylight: sunset from the water, and plankton that glows once it is dark.

The boat leaves from the fish sculpture plaza on Ao Nang beach and heads out to Koh Daeng, one of the smaller islands off the Krabi coast that day tours generally skip. Snorkelling comes first while there is still light, with masks provided and the guide pointing out where the reef is worth your time. As the sun goes down the limestone stacks around the bay turn from grey to copper, which is the part most people book the trip for without realising it.

After dark the boat moves to sheltered water for the plankton swim. The light comes from dinoflagellates reacting to movement, so it appears around your hands and feet rather than across the surface. It is genuinely unpredictable: dark nights near the new moon give the strongest display, bright moonlight washes it out, and rough water scatters it. If seeing it matters to you, choose a date close to a new moon.

LoveLay Andaman runs this trip and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers pick-up transfer, a professional guide, seasonal fruit, drinking water, snorkelling mask and insurance.

Bring a towel and dry clothes. Five hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Koh Daeng, skipped by most day tours
Snorkelling in daylight, plankton after dark
Sunset over the limestone stacks from the water
Strongest display on dark nights near the new moon
Pick-up, guide, mask, fruit and water included

fullDescription:
A half-day among the mangroves at Tung Yee Peng, a fishing village on Ko Lanta that runs its own community tourism rather than selling the trip to outside operators.

The boat is a traditional longtail, which matters here: the shallow draught lets it work its way into channels that a speedboat cannot enter. Mangrove forest is not scenic in the obvious way a beach is, and that is the point of going with a guide. You are looking at a nursery, where the tangled prop roots shelter juvenile fish, crabs and mudskippers before they move out to the reef, and at a system that absorbs storm surge for the island behind it. Kingfishers and monitor lizards are common, and the water sits almost still, so the whole trip is quiet in a way boat tours rarely are.

Tung Yee Peng itself is a Muslim fishing community with a raised boardwalk through the forest and seafood that comes off local boats. Lunch is included and eaten in the village.

This is the right trip for a rainy or windy day. Mangrove channels are sheltered water, so it runs in conditions that close the open-sea island tours during the green season from May to October.

Oh-Hoo runs this excursion and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers hotel round-trip transfer, lunch with drinking water and fruit, a life jacket, a local English-speaking guide and basic accident insurance.

Four hours, departing on Ko Lanta, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Longtail boat into channels speedboats cannot reach
Tung Yee Peng, a community-run fishing village
Mangrove nursery: mudskippers, crabs, kingfishers
Sheltered water, so it runs when island trips are cancelled
Village lunch, guide and transfers included

fullDescription:
Krabi Town and a beach ride in one half-day, for people basing themselves in Ao Nang who have not yet seen the province beyond it.

Most visitors treat Krabi as a departure point for boats and never go into the town itself, which sits 20 kilometres inland on the river. It is a working provincial capital rather than a resort: a riverside walkway, a morning market, and Wat Kaew Korawaram sitting white above a long flight of steps. The scale is small and the pace is ordinary, and that contrast with Ao Nang is the reason to go.

The horse ride is an hour on the sand, arranged so the horses work in the cooler part of the day. No riding experience is assumed and the handlers stay with you throughout; the pace is a walk with the option of more if you are comfortable. Riding on a beach with the karsts offshore is the kind of thing that photographs far better than it sounds.

Anda Krabi Seatour runs this and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers hotel pick-up and drop-off, the one-hour horse ride, the city tour and a local guide. Tips are not included, so budget for those separately.

Three and a half hours in total, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Krabi Town, which most Ao Nang visitors never see
Wat Kaew Korawaram and the riverside walkway
One hour on horseback along the beach
No riding experience needed, handlers stay with you
Hotel pick-up, drop-off and local guide included
